answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x with a release 2h ago and latency rising for 90m, so a bad build is the most specific new cause, and memory_b1 is the closest prior fix. Peak settlement writes are expected daily, so load alone is not uniquely explanatory; memory_b5 is the competing write-latency story (primary overloaded by reads) and should be checked before locking the choice. Circuit breaking is rejected because memory_b4 is fail-fast and would drop customer writes, which violates the objective. Rollback during heavy settlement can still jeopardize in-flight writes, so keep it a small guarded cohort rather than a fleet-wide revert until the two archives confirm which mechanism actually applied. Regional failover and extra capacity remain unchosen: no regional signal, and headroom-after-the-fact is slower and may not fix a regressing build.
